mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.75% compresses discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Fed maintains accommodative policy during economic stress.
failure_condition: The proportion of positive 20-day SPX returns following months with FEDFUNDS < 0.75% is less than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals accelerating labor market deterioration, triggering negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as recession fears intensify.
failure_condition: The proportion of positive 5-day SPX returns following a 3-month UNRATE increase > 0.5pp is greater than 60%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in retail sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as economic activity weakens.
failure_condition: In months where RSAFS and HOUST both decline from the prior month, the SPX 60-day return is negative in less than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing supply shock (INDPRO decline > 1% from prior month) reduces corporate production capacity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: The proportion of positive 20-day SPX returns during supply shocks (INDPRO decline > 1% from prior month) is greater than 60%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer spending growth (RSAFS monthly increase > 0.5%) signals robust economic activity, generating positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as corporate earnings expectations rise.
failure_condition: The proportion of positive 5-day SPX returns following months with RSAFS growth > 0.5% is less than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: A CPIAUCSL monthly inflation rate exceeding 0.3% signals accelerating price pressures, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as the Fed is expected to tighten policy.
failure_condition: The proportion of negative 60-day SPX returns following a CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.3% is less than 40%.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in employment (PAYEMS) and unemployment rate increases (UNRATE) indicate severe labor market distress, driving negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days as recession risks escalate.
failure_condition: In months where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises from the prior month, the SPX 5-day return is negative in less than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: During low interest rate environments (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), accommodative monetary policy supports equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days as risk appetite increases.
failure_condition: In periods with FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, the proportion of positive 60-day SPX returns is less than 40%.
